project: [Feature Flag Smith Feature Tasks Kanban Enabled Prd] Feature-gated Kanban visibility
overview: As an operator, I want the Tasks Kanban view available only when enabled so unfinished workflow UX does not appear by default.
goals: Hide Tasks Kanban by default unless a dedicated feature flag is enabled.
Provide deterministic flag evaluation so UI behavior is consistent per environment.
Ensure operators can verify enabled versus disabled behavior through observable signals and tests.
nonGoals: Redesigning the Tasks Kanban experience itself.
Changing task data model semantics unrelated to visibility gating.
Introducing user-level rollout targeting in this phase.
successMetrics: When the feature flag is disabled, Tasks Kanban navigation and route are inaccessible in all operator sessions.
When the feature flag is enabled, Tasks Kanban navigation and route are available and render as expected.
Automated checks cover both enabled and disabled states with no regressions in existing task views.
rules: Tasks Kanban visibility must be controlled exclusively by a single feature flag evaluation path.
Disabled state must prevent both navigation entry points and direct route access.
Enabled state must preserve existing authorization boundaries for task views.
Feature flag defaults to disabled unless explicitly enabled by configuration.

blockers.description: Unable to execute full quality gates in this workspace because required tooling is missing: `go` (`go test ./...`), `docker`, and `act`.

stories.title: Define canonical feature flag contract for Tasks Kanban
stories.description: As an operator, I want a clearly defined feature flag key and default behavior so Kanban visibility is predictable across environments.
acceptanceCriteria: A single documented flag key controls Tasks Kanban visibility.
Default evaluation returns disabled when configuration is absent.
Example: with no flag configured, Kanban is hidden and no Kanban route is exposed.
Negative case: invalid flag values are handled safely and resolve to disabled.

stories.title: Gate Tasks Kanban navigation entry points behind the feature flag
stories.description: As an operator, I want Kanban links and controls hidden when disabled so unfinished UX does not appear by default.
acceptanceCriteria: All UI entry points to Tasks Kanban are conditionally rendered based on the feature flag.
Example: when disabled, navigation menus do not display any Kanban option.
Example: when enabled, Kanban option is visible and selectable.
Negative case: stale cached UI state does not surface Kanban after reload when flag is disabled.

stories.title: Protect direct Tasks Kanban route access when the feature is disabled
stories.description: As an operator, I want direct URL access to Kanban blocked when disabled so hidden UX cannot be reached by deep links.
acceptanceCriteria: Direct navigation to the Kanban route checks the feature flag before rendering.
Example: when disabled, direct Kanban URL redirects to a safe fallback view.
Example: when enabled, direct Kanban URL loads normally.
Negative case: browser back/forward navigation cannot bypass the disabled-state gate.

stories.title: Expose operational visibility of feature flag state
stories.description: As an operator, I want observable signals for Kanban flag evaluation so troubleshooting visibility behavior is fast and reliable.
acceptanceCriteria: Flag evaluation outcome is logged or surfaced through existing diagnostics without leaking sensitive data.
Example: startup or request-level diagnostics indicate whether Kanban flag is enabled or disabled.
Negative case: missing configuration still produces a clear disabled-state diagnostic.

stories.title: Add automated coverage for enabled and disabled Kanban states
stories.description: As an operator, I want automated tests validating both flag states so regressions do not re-expose unfinished Kanban UX.
acceptanceCriteria: Test coverage verifies Kanban navigation and route are hidden when the flag is disabled.
Test coverage verifies Kanban navigation and route are available when the flag is enabled.
Negative case: tests fail if Kanban renders in disabled mode or is inaccessible in enabled mode.
